[#secure-performance]
== The guard's cost

Every function of webcpp that computes on a secret (a MAC, a key derivation, a tag's
comparison, a cipher) runs inside `timing_guard`, which on 64-bit ARM under macOS, iOS,
Linux, Android and Windows, where the CPU has FEAT_DIT, sets DIT (data-independent
timing) for the call and restores the thread's state after it (<<secure-guard>>): one
`mrs`; where DIT was clear, two `msr` each followed by an `isb`; where it was set, a
second `mrs` on the way out (and an `msr` if something inside cleared it). Elsewhere
(x86, WebAssembly, ARM64EC) it executes no instruction. A function keyed only by its
arguments, called without a key, holds a disengaged guard, which reads its flag and
does nothing else.

Measured natively on 2026-11-26 (UTC) on Apple M5 Max
(arm64), Darwin 27.0.0, built with variant=release
by Apple LLVM 21.0.0 (clang-2100.4.1.1) (bench/timing.cpp): each row is the median of
5 runs of 10,000,000 guards around a store, with the
fastest and slowest run beside it, each minus the median of the same loop without the
guard, in nanoseconds per call; a figure that rounds to zero or below, the loop's
noise, shows as 0.0.
The guard sets DIT on this machine. The machine's 1, 5 and 15 minute load averages were 1.88/2.73/3.21
before and 1.88/2.73/3.21 after, on 18 cores: the figures
are to be taken on an idle machine, one whose 1 minute load average is below 2.

[cols="2,4,1,1,1",options="header"]
